verdicts.title: Complexity of the CNF-satisfiability problem
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: This paper is devoted to the complexity of the Boolean satisfiability problem. We consider a version of this problem, where the Boolean formula is specified in the conjunctive normal form. We prove an unexpected result that the CNF-satisfiability problem can be solved by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract makes a sweeping (and dubious) claim that 'CNF-satisfiability problem can be solved by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time,' which concerns SAT decision complexity, not resolution width lower bounds via fatgraph genus. It does not address ribbon graphs, embedding genus, or resolution refutation width.

verdicts.title: Graph Width Measures for CNF-Encodings with Auxiliary Variables
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We consider bounded width CNF-formulas where the width is measured by popular graph width measures on graphs associated to CNF-formulas. It shares the 'width on CNF graph' vocabulary but does not interact with the specific claim that fatgraph genus lower-bounds resolution width.

verdicts.title: Regular resolution for CNFs with almost bounded one-sided treewidth
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We introduce a one-sided incidence tree decomposition of a CNF $\varphi$. This is a tree decomposition of the incidence graph of $\varphi$ where the underlying tree is rooted and the set of bags containing each clause induces a directed path in the tree. The one-sided treewidth is the smallest width of a one-sided incidence tree decomposition.
